# Workspace Instructions

- For any time-based scheduling, waiting, market-open planning, or delayed-launch command, always check the local machine time and effective UTC offset first instead of asking the user what time it is.
- Treat terminal timestamps, launcher timestamps, and run artifact timestamps as local machine time unless the source explicitly says UTC or another timezone.
- When discussing schedules, logs, or trading windows in this workspace, always convert local machine time to Beijing time (`Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC+8`) and use Beijing time as the default business reference.
- For China domestic futures in this workspace, assume Beijing trading windows by default unless a specific exchange/product rule overrides them: day session `09:00-10:15`, `10:30-11:30`, `13:30-15:00`; if Beijing time is between `11:30` and `13:30`, the next day-session open is `13:30` the same day, not the night session.
- For contracts with night trading, treat `21:00` Beijing as the night-session start by default, and remember that the close varies by product (`23:00`, `23:30`, `01:00`, or `02:30`). If the exact product matters, verify the exchange/product-specific night close instead of assuming one universal end time.
- Do not tell the user to wait until the evening when the next upcoming Beijing session is the same-day afternoon session at `13:30`.
- When useful, provide both times in one sentence: `local machine time -> Beijing time`.
- If the machine is in US Eastern time, account for daylight saving automatically by checking the effective current offset rather than assuming fixed `EST = UTC-5`.
- Do not require the user to repeat the current local time or ask for manual timezone clarification when the machine time can be checked directly.
- Before adding code, patches, or new modules for any substantial vn.py engineering task, first comprehensively scan the official vn.py sources and ecosystem in this order: the official org repo index https://github.com/vnpy?tab=repositories, the core repo https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy, and the official docs https://www.vnpy.com/docs/cn/index.html. Prefer adopting and integrating official implementations when available; only build custom code after confirming the official stack does not already provide the needed capability.
- For gateway work, check the matching official gateway repo under the vnpy org first, especially https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_ctp and other gateway repos listed under https://github.com/vnpy?tab=repositories.
- For strategy/app-level work, check the official app repos first, especially https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_ctastrategy, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_ctabacktester, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_paperaccount, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_riskmanager, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_datamanager, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_datarecorder, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_spreadtrading, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_portfoliostrategy, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_algotrading, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_scripttrader, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_optionmaster, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_webtrader, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_portfoliomanager, and https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_rpcservice.
- For database/datafeed/supporting capability work, check the relevant official repos first, especially https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_sqlite, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_mysql, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_postgresql, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_mongodb, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_dolphindb, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_taos, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_rqdata, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_xt, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_tushare, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_tqsdk, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_wind, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_ifind, https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_rest, and https://github.com/vnpy/vnpy_websocket.
